findings.evidence: Bead jade-lnn.1, description: 'A script that generates CODE_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET and the backup encryption key on the server'. Its acceptance: 'writes them only to the app's env file'. phase-10-production-deploy.md line 41 (p10-secrets): 'Generate production secrets on the server'. So the backup encryption key is on the production VM's disk, next to the plaintext DB volume and CODE_PEPPER. The plan's threat model says otherwise. TB5: 'encrypted dump; key held offline'. AB14 'Theft of a backup or the VM disk': 'Encrypted backups, key offline (jade-6o3, jade-lnn.1, jade-fgs); pepper not in the dump (jade-fd5; ADR 0011)', verified by 'jade-6o3 restore drill'. The SECRETS_ENV node is labelled only 'CODE_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET'. Failure scenario: someone who obtains the VM disk (provider snapshot, decommissioned volume, host compromise) gets the DB, the pepper (so offline guessing of every kit code from code_hmac, which ADR 0011's pepper is meant to prevent) and the backup key (so all 30 days of backups, including data already deleted from the live DB). None of AB14's named mitigations applies to that half of the case. p9-authz-sweep (jade-sio) would mark AB14 verified by a restore drill that tests nothing about it. This breaks OB5 for AB14 and the rubric rule that every claim must be one the sources support. Also, no source says whether the key on the VM can decrypt or only encrypt, and the plan picks 'offline' without saying so (INV6).
findings.fix: Label SECRETS_ENV 'env file: CODE_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET, backup encryption key (jade-lnn.1)', and give the 'Other secrets' asset that location. Reword TB5: the key is generated on the VM and written to the env file (jade-lnn.1), with copies in the offline store (jade-fgs), and whether the copy on the VM can decrypt backups is not specified. Split AB14: (a) theft of a backup, with the current mitigations; (b) theft of the VM disk or compromise of the host, which exposes the DB, the pepper and the backup key. Name the mitigations that do exist, such as p10-prod-infra jade-dvm (firewall, SSH restricted, security updates, Phase 10), and provider and disk handling as open until jade-0za. Add a TM item saying no source covers encryption at rest of the VM disk or keeping the pepper and backup key off the disk, and keep the AC9 constraints (every mitigation id in the Phase cell).
